title: Choosing the Right Test — Five Patients, Five Decisions

hook.en: Knowing what each test shows is only half the skill. The other half is picking the right one for the right patient at the right time. Work through five common cases that pull together X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, ECG, lab and lung tests.
hook.ur: Har test kya dikhata hai yeh jaanna aadhi maharat hai. Doosri aadhi sahi mareez ke liye sahi waqt par sahi test chunna hai. Paanch aam kes hal karein jo X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, ECG, lab aur phephron ke tests ko milate hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll match a clinical question to the best first test, explain why other tests are not the first choice, know when a test result means treat, refer or wait, and communicate the plan to the patient.
goal.ur: End tak aap clinical sawal ko behtareen pehle test se milayenge, samjhayenge ke doosre tests pehli pasand kyun nahi, jaanenge ke test ka nateeja ilaj, refer ya intezaar ka kya matlab hai, aur plan mareez ko batayenge.

text.en: Choosing a test starts with the **question**, not the machine. Ask: **What am I trying to find out? What would I do differently with each answer? What is the safest, quickest, most useful test to answer it?** Then match the test to the **tissue and the question**: bone and fractures (X-ray, CT), soft tissue and nerves (MRI, ultrasound), the heart's rhythm and muscle (ECG, echo), the lungs (chest X-ray, spirometry, blood gas), and the body's chemistry (blood tests). The most useful test is **the one whose result would change what you do**.
text.ur: Test chunna **sawal** se shuru hota hai, machine se nahi. Poochhein: **Main kya jaanna chahta hoon? Har jawab par mein kya alag karunga? Isay jawab dene ke liye sab se mehfooz, tez, mufeed test kaun sa hai?** Phir test ko **tissue aur sawal** se milayein: haddi aur fractures (X-ray, CT), narm tissue aur nerves (MRI, ultrasound), dil ki rhythm aur muscle (ECG, echo), phephre (chest X-ray, spirometry, blood gas), aur jism ki chemistry (blood tests). Sab se mufeed test **woh hai jis ka nateeja aap ka kaam badal de**.

text.en: Think of tests as **tools in a toolbox**. A hammer is perfect for a nail and useless for a screw. A good tradesperson does not reach for the biggest tool every time: they ask what the job is first. Likewise, an MRI is excellent for a torn meniscus and useless for finding a rhythm problem. The skill is matching the tool to the job.
text.ur: Tests ko **auzaar ke dabbay ke auzaar** samjhein. Hathora keel ke liye behtareen aur screw ke liye bekaar hai. Achha mistri har baar sab se bara auzaar nahi uthata: pehle poochhta hai kaam kya hai. Isi tarah MRI phati meniscus ke liye behtareen hai aur rhythm ke masle ke liye bekaar. Maharat auzaar ko kaam se milana hai.

title.en: A way to choose in five steps
title.ur: Paanch qadam mein chunne ka tareeqa

steps.title: Name the question
steps.detail: Is it a fracture? A clot? A torn tendon? An abnormal heart rhythm? Poor lung function? Infection? Write the one question the test must answer. || Sawal ka naam likhein

steps.title: Check for red flags and rules
steps.detail: Use decision rules where they exist (Ottawa, Canadian C-spine, back pain red flags). If a red flag is present, refer for urgent assessment instead of choosing a test yourself. || Red flags aur rules dekhein

steps.title: Match the tissue
steps.detail: Bone: X-ray first, CT for detail. Soft tissue: ultrasound for superficial structures and movement, MRI for deep ones. Heart: ECG then echo. Lungs: chest X-ray, spirometry, blood gas. Chemistry and infection: blood tests. || Tissue milayein

steps.title: Decide what the result will change
steps.detail: If every result leads to the same plan, the test is not needed. Decide in advance: treat, modify, refer or wait. Then explain the choice and the plan to the patient. || Faisla karein nateeja kya badlega

question.en: A 55-year-old has a locked knee after a twist. Which investigation is most useful?
question.ur: 55 saal ke mareez ka mur ne ke baad knee lock ho gaya hai. Kaun si investigation sab se mufeed hai?

feedback.en: That does not help a knee.

text.en: An MRI of the knee after an X-ray to exclude a fracture
text.ur: Fracture rule out karne ke X-ray ke baad knee ka MRI

feedback.en: Yes — a locked knee suggests a mechanical block such as a meniscal tear.
feedback.ur: Haan — lock hui knee meniscal tear jaisi mechanical rukawat batati hai.

title.ur: Kaun sa test kis sawal ke liye?

rows.en: Compression ultrasound (and the doctor's clot score)
rows.ur: Compression ultrasound (aur doctor ka clot score)

rows.en: Stop, ECG and urgent medical review
rows.ur: Rukein, ECG aur foran medical review
COPD mein saans ki tangi aur neend

rows.en: Arterial blood gas and chest X-ray
rows.ur: Arterial blood gas aur chest X-ray

text.en: **Question, red flag, tissue, change.** Name the question, check for red flags and rules, match the tissue, and ask what the result will change. If nothing, do not test.
text.ur: **Sawal, red flag, tissue, tabdeeli.** Sawal likhein, red flags aur rules dekhein, tissue milayein, aur poochhein nateeja kya badlega. Kuch nahi to test na karein.

text.en: **Asking for the most advanced test first.** An MRI before an X-ray in a possible fracture, or a CT for an ordinary sprain, adds cost, time and sometimes radiation, and can miss the simple answer. Start with the simplest test that answers the question, and escalate when it does not.
text.ur: **Sab se jadeed test pehle maangna.** Mumkin fracture mein X-ray se pehle MRI, ya aam moch ke liye CT, kharch, waqt aur kabhi radiation barhata hai, aur saada jawab miss kar sakta hai. Sawal ka jawab dene wala saada test pehle karein, aur jab na ho to barhayein.

question.en: A 68-year-old man reports chest pain and breathlessness while walking in rehabilitation, and his lips look pale. What do you do first?
question.ur: 68 saal ka mareez rehabilitation mein chalte hue seene ka dard aur saans ki tangi batata hai, aur honth zard hain. Aap pehle kya karein?

text.en: Stop, sit him down, check vital signs and call the medical team for an urgent ECG
text.ur: Rukein, bithayein, vital signs check karein aur urgent ECG ke liye medical team ko bulayein

feedback.en: Yes — safety first, then the right test with the doctor.
feedback.ur: Haan — pehle hifazat, phir doctor ke saath sahi test.

text.en: Continue the session at a lower speed
text.ur: Kam raftar par session jaari rakhein

text.en: Book a lung function test for next week
text.ur: Agle haftay phephron ke function test ka intezam karein

feedback.en: It is an emergency, not a routine problem.
feedback.ur: Yeh emergency hai, routine masla nahi.

question.en: A patient with 3 weeks of mechanical low back pain and no red flags asks for a scan. What is the best choice?
question.ur: Mareez ko 3 haftay se mechanical kamar dard hai aur red flags nahi, woh scan maangta hai. Behtareen intikhab kya hai?

text.en: No scan; explain, treat actively and review
text.ur: Scan nahi; samjhayein, active ilaj karein aur review

feedback.en: Yes — a scan would not change the plan.

feedback.ur: Yeh faida ke baghair radiation barhata hai.

text.en: **Tell the patient what you are choosing and why.** For example: "I am not asking for an MRI because your examination shows no warning signs, and a scan would probably show normal age-related changes that do not change your treatment. If your pain changes or you develop weakness or numbness, we will act straight away." Patients accept this when it is clear and the follow-up is certain.
text.ur: **Mareez ko batayein aap kya chun rahe hain aur kyun.** Maslan: "Main MRI nahi maang raha kyunke aap ke examination mein warning signs nahi, aur scan shayad umar ke mutabiq normal tabdeeliyan dikhayega jo aap ka ilaj nahi badlengi. Dard badle ya kamzori ya sunn hona ho to hum foran kaarwai karenge." Mareez isay qabool karte hain jab saaf ho aur follow-up yaqeeni.

question.en: Why can an earlier, simpler test be better than a more detailed one?
question.ur: Pehle, saada test zyada tafseeli test se behtar kyun ho sakta hai?

answer.en: A simpler test often answers the main question faster, more cheaply and with less risk, and the result tells you whether a second, more detailed test is needed. Starting with the most detailed test can bury the answer in findings that do not matter, and can delay action.
answer.ur: Saada test aksar mukhya sawal ka jawab tez, sasta aur kam khatre ke saath deta hai, aur nateeja batata hai ke doosre, zyada tafseeli test ki zaroorat hai ya nahi. Sab se tafseeli test se shuru karna jawab ko ghair ahem findings mein dafan kar sakta hai aur kaarwai mein takheer kar sakta hai.

beats.patient: A 45-year-old woman is breathless on exertion and has a swollen, painful left calf, 10 days after a long flight. She has no chest pain at rest. Her oxygen level is 94 percent and her heart rate is 105.
beats.assessment: A swollen, painful calf after travel with breathlessness raises the concern of a clot in the leg that may have travelled to the lung. This is a medical emergency, not a physiotherapy decision.
beats.treatment: Stop exercise, keep her rested, record her observations and ask for same-day medical assessment (an ultrasound of the leg and further tests are likely).
beats.reassess: She is assessed urgently and a clot is found and treated.

text.en: **When in doubt, escalate.** Choosing the right test is the doctor's job; yours is to notice, protect, document and refer quickly. Never delay care to wait for a scan, and never start or progress exercise in a patient with unexplained chest pain, breathlessness, a swollen painful calf, new neurological signs or a possible fracture until the medical team has reviewed.
text.ur: **Shak ho to escalate karein.** Sahi test chunna doctor ka kaam hai; aap ka kaam dekhna, bachana, likhna aur jald refer karna hai. Scan ke intezaar mein care mein takheer na karein, aur be-wajah seene ke dard, saans ki tangi, soojhi dardnak pindli, nayi neurological nishaniyon ya mumkin fracture wale mareez mein medical team ke review se pehle exercise shuru ya tez na karein.

summary.en: Start with the question, check red flags and decision rules, match the tissue to the test and ask what the result will change.
summary.ur: Sawal se shuru karein, red flags aur decision rules dekhein, tissue ko test se milayein aur poochhein nateeja kya badlega.

summary.en: Use the simplest test that answers the question; escalate to more detailed tests only when needed.
summary.ur: Sawal ka jawab dene wala saada test istemal karein; zaroorat par hi zyada tafseeli tests ki taraf barhein.

summary.en: Explain your choice and follow-up to the patient, and escalate promptly when a red flag or emergency picture appears.
summary.ur: Apna intikhab aur follow-up mareez ko samjhayein, aur red flag ya emergency tasveer par jald escalate karein.

back.ur: Yeh kharch aur khatra barhata hai aur jawab dafan kar sakta hai; saada test aksar sawal ka jawab deta hai.
